content_html:
A TUI dashboard for managing multiple AI coding sessions running in the terminal emulator or multiplexer of your choice, such as Kitty and zellij.

captain-miao.demo.mp4

When you run several agent sessions at once, it's hard to tell which is working, which is waiting on you, and which has already finished. captain-miao watches every session and shows the whole fleet at a glance (status, working directory, context usage, and a live preview), and lets you start, focus, fork, or kill any of them without leaving the dashboard.

Unlike herdr or cmux, captain-miao embeds no terminal of its own. It drives the Kitty or zellij you already run (every session is a native window or pane, controlled through the terminal's own protocol), so it stays one small, focused tool and the rest of your workflow is yours to compose.

Highlights

  • The whole fleet at a glance: every session in one table, with status, working directory, model, context usage, git branch, and a live transcript preview.
  • Never miss a prompt: sessions waiting on your approval or an answer are flagged.
  • Full session lifecycle: launch, resume, fork, and kill sessions from the dashboard, with a filterable picker for recent working directories.
  • Support Claude Code and Codex today, behind a backend abstraction built to extend to other coding agents.
  • direnv-aware: a session started in a directory with an .envrc picks up that environment automatically (via direnv exec).
  • r3 integration: when a session's running background task is an r3 watch waiting for your review, it flags as Review and surfaces as needing your attention.
  • Keep-awake: prevents your machine from sleeping while any session is still working (caffeinate on macOS, systemd-inhibit on Linux).
  • Pin, mute, mark: pin important sessions to the top, mute the ones you don't need right now, and flag the ones to follow up on.
  • Sessions that outlive their window (opt-in): run them in a local pty pool so closing the terminal — or logging out — doesn't end them, and a dashboard on another machine can attach to the same ones.

Requirements

  • A supported terminal: Kitty with remote control enabled (see Kitty setup), or zellij ≥ 0.44 (run captain-miao inside the zellij session; no extra setup needed).
  • Claude Code and/or Codex on your PATH.

Installation

From source with Cargo

cargo install --git https://github.com/hyperlogue/captain-miao

This installs the miao command (the project is captain-miao; the binary is short because you'll type it a lot).

Building needs a Rust toolchain and a C compiler (for the statically-bundled SQLite that reads Codex session titles).

From a prebuilt binary (npm)

No Rust toolchain, no build:

npx @hyperlogue/captain-miao          # run it once
npm install -g @hyperlogue/captain-miao   # or install the `miao` command

bunx @hyperlogue/captain-miao works too. The npm package is a small launcher that execs a prebuilt native binary shipped as a per-platform optional dependency, so your package manager downloads only the one binary matching your machine; nothing is fetched at runtime. Prebuilt binaries cover macOS (Apple silicon + Intel) and Linux (x86-64 + arm64), and are also attached to every GitHub Release as a .tar.gz if you'd rather download one directly.

With Nix

A flake is provided; run it straight from GitHub:

nix run github:hyperlogue/captain-miao

Kitty setup

captain-miao drives Kitty over its remote-control protocol, so your kitty.conf must allow it. Remote control is a real privilege (a program that has it can read your terminal and run commands), so the tightest setup kitty offers pairs a password with an authorization script:

allow_remote_control password
remote_control_password "i-am-the-captain-miao" captain_miao_rc.py
listen_on unix:/tmp/mykitty

Kitty resolves that filename against your config directory, so put the script at ~/.config/kitty/captain_miao_rc.py:

# The only remote-control commands captain-miao issues.
ALLOWED_COMMANDS = frozenset({
    "ls", "get-text", "launch", "focus-window",
    "focus-tab", "close-window", "detach-window", "goto-layout",
})

def is_cmd_allowed(pcmd, window, from_socket, extra_data):
    # Reject the in-terminal escape-code channel; only the listen_on socket gets in.
    return from_socket and pcmd["cmd"] in ALLOWED_COMMANDS

Every request must now clear three checks: arrive over the socket (not the escape-code channel that a shell, even one across ssh, could otherwise use), carry the password, and name one of the commands above. i-am-the-captain-miao is captain-miao's built-in default, so this works as written; to use your own secret instead, set remote_control_password (above) and [kitty] rc_password in captain-miao's config to match. Keep the script the last item after the password; command names listed alongside it are allowed without ever calling your function.

Looser alternatives: allow_remote_control socket-only (off the escape-code channel, but no password and no allowlist) or allow_remote_control yes (no checks at all; avoid it). captain-miao verifies remote control at startup and exits with a diagnostic if it can't connect.

Keep the stack layout enabled. captain-miao's default Stacked session layout puts every session in one kitty tab and shows one at a time via kitty's stack layout. The default enabled_layouts * already includes it; if you've narrowed that list, add stack or sessions tile instead of stacking. (The alternate Per-tab layout, toggled with Space l, needs no particular layout.)

Usage

Run the dashboard inside a supported terminal (Kitty or zellij):

miao

miao must be launched from within Kitty or a zellij session; it exits with an error otherwise. When run inside a zellij session it auto-selects the zellij backend (override with [terminal] backend in the config).

From the dashboard, o / O start new sessions and r resumes existing ones. You can also drive captain-miao from the shell:

Command What it does
miao Run the TUI dashboard (the default).
miao claude [dir] [args…] Launch Claude Code in dir (default .) with tracking hooks. Args starting with - (e.g. --resume) are forwarded straight to claude.
miao codex [dir] [args…] Launch Codex in dir with tracking hooks; extra args are forwarded to codex.
miao focus [--window-id <id>] Focus the running dashboard window; with --window-id, also ring the session running in that Kitty window.
miao hook <event> Internal: forwards an agent hook event to the launcher. You won't run this yourself; it's wired up automatically.

Sessions launched via claude / codex are wrapped by a launcher process that injects the tracking hooks, so they show up in the dashboard automatically. Hooks are injected per-session and torn down on exit; nothing is written to your global ~/.claude/settings.json.

Key bindings

Press ? in the dashboard for the complete list. Highlights:

Key Action
j/k, ↑/↓, Ctrl-n/p Navigate sessions
gg / G Jump to top / bottom
1..9 / Ctrl-1..9 Select Nth session / select and focus its window
Enter Focus the selected session's window
o / O New session (same tab / prompt for cwd)
r / f Resume picker (one host; Ctrl-h switches) / fork the selected session
x / D Kill the selected session / detach from it, leaving it running
s Jump to the next session needing attention
m / p / i Mute / pin / toggle needs-input on the selected session
y Copy the selected session id to the clipboard
t / w Move window to tab (Kitty only) / switch to or open the cwd's work tab
h/l, ←/→ Scroll the preview horizontally
Ctrl-u / Ctrl-d Scroll the preview up / down
R Refresh the preview now
Space v / Space d Toggle the preview / detail panel
Space i Edit the selected directory's icon + color
Space e / Space E Restart the selected / all idle sessions
Space z Toggle keep-awake (inhibit OS sleep while sessions work)
Space a / Space H Set the default backend / default host for new sessions
Space l Switch session layout (stacked in one tab / one tab per session)
Space h / Space s Hosts panel / attach to a session, kicking the client holding it
? Show the full key list (help overlay)
/ Search
q / Ctrl-c Quit

Pressing Space (the leader) shows a which-key strip of the available follow-up keys in the footer.

In the cwd picker, Ctrl-t switches the backend for that one launch, Ctrl-h the host, and Ctrl-d drops the highlighted recent directory.

Custom keybindings. Every Normal-mode command above is remappable via a [keybinds] table in ~/.config/captain-miao/config.toml. Map a command id to a key (or list of keys); an empty list unbinds it:

[keybinds]
kill = "X"                      # move kill from x to X
jump_attention = ["s", "n"]     # bind two keys to one command
restart = "space r"             # remap a leader sequence
toggle_detail = []              # unbind a command

Keys parse forms like "ctrl+u", "O" (= "shift+o"), "space e", "enter", "f5", and arrow names. Ctrl-c, g g, and the 1..9 / Ctrl-1..9 selectors are fixed.

Command ids are the string in each Command::id(); the authoritative list lives in the DEFAULTS table in src/app/keymap.rs, and they match the actions in the key-bindings table above.

Configuration

captain-miao reads an optional TOML file at ~/.config/captain-miao/config.toml (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/captain-miao/config.toml). Every key is optional and falls back to the default shown below; an unparseable file falls back to defaults rather than crashing. The complete set of options:

[terminal]
backend = "kitty"            # "kitty" | "zellij"; unset auto-detects (zellij inside a zellij session, else Kitty)
sessions_layout = "stacked"  # "stacked" | "per-tab" (the runtime Space l toggle overrides this)

[kitty]
rc_password = "i-am-the-captain-miao"   # the built-in default, and a published constant; set your own (see Kitty setup)

[launcher]
default_agent = "claude"     # backend for new sessions: "claude" | "codex" (Space a overrides)
approval_grace_secs = 2      # grace window after a permission dialog before a transcript change reads as "dismissed"
max_recent_cwds = 50         # entries kept in the workdir picker's recent list
resume_list_limit = 200      # max sessions listed in the resume picker
new_tab_title = "{agent}: {basename}"     # new-session tab title; placeholders: {agent} {basename} {cwd}
resume_tab_title = "{agent}: {basename}"  # resumed-session tab title
pooled = false               # run this machine's sessions in the local pty pool (see below)

[thresholds]
context_warning_tokens = 175000    # context usage turns to the warning color here
context_critical_tokens = 400000   # …and to the critical color here
preview_stale_secs = 20            # show "updated Ns ago" once the preview is older than this (0 = always)

[polling]
fs_reload_debounce_ms = 100        # debounce for filesystem-watch reloads
preview_debounce_ms = 200          # debounce before re-fetching the preview
event_poll_ms = 100                # input poll interval (floored at 10)
preview_auto_refresh_secs = 10     # auto-refresh the preview while focused + busy + unscrolled (0 disables)

[ui.panels]
preview_auto_min_height = 16       # min body height before the preview auto-shows
detail_auto_min_width = 70         # min body width before the detail panel auto-shows
detail_default_width = 36          # detail panel column width
narrow_max_width = 90              # at/below this body width the layout stacks vertically

[ui.table]
name_truncate = 35                 # max characters of a session name before truncation

[colors.ui]
title_fg = "cyan"
header_fg = "cyan"
attention_fg = "yellow"
error_fg = "red"
highlight_bg = "dark_gray"
selection_fg = "blue"
selection_symbol = "❯ "

[colors.picker]
highlight_bg = "dark_gray"
chevron_fg = "blue"

[debug]
enabled = false                    # verbose logging; also enabled by CAPTAIN_MIAO_DEBUG=1
log_file = "debug.log"
keybind_log_file = "keybinds.log"

[keybinds]
# Remap any Normal-mode command: command-id = "key" or ["key", "alt"]; [] unbinds.
# command-ids are the Command::id() strings in src/app/keymap.rs (DEFAULTS table).
# e.g. kill = "X"  /  jump_attention = ["s", "n"]  /  restart = "space r"

Colors accept named values (cyan, dark_gray, …) or #rrggbb hex. The command ids for [keybinds] are the ones in the key-bindings table above (kill, jump_attention, restart, toggle_preview, …).

Pooled sessions ([launcher] pooled)

By default a session is its terminal window: closing the window ends it. With pooled = true captain-miao instead runs each session in a local pty pool (an embedded libshpool), and the window merely attaches to it — so the session survives closing the window, a crashed multiplexer, and logging out.

This is meant for dev servers, not laptops. On a machine you only ever sit at, the pool buys no persistence and costs an extra process hop, no scrollback replay when you reattach, and one client at a time. On a machine you also reach from elsewhere it's the point: a dashboard on your laptop and a captain-miao you ssh into from a phone become two clients of the same sessions.

Needs miao-server on PATH (it hosts the pool); without it the dashboard says so and falls back to the default behaviour. On Linux, also run loginctl enable-linger — see below.

Running sessions on other machines

Remote-host support is behind a cargo feature while it's being verified; build with cargo build --release --features remote, then add hosts with Space h. Each host runs a miao-server daemon holding its sessions in a pty pool, and the dashboard attaches local windows to them over ssh, so a dropped connection or a slept laptop detaches windows without touching the sessions — and reconnecting brings them all back. Full design notes: docs/remote-sessions.md.

Getting the daemon onto each host. Either install miao-server there yourself (any copy on PATH matching your dashboard's version is used as is, and never touched), or let the dashboard carry one and deploy it for you:

# Download this version's published servers and bundle them in — needs only
# curl and tar, no cross toolchain:
cargo xtask dist --variant bundle-linux --from release

# …or cross-compile them from the sources beside you, which is what you want
# while changing the server itself:
nix develop                                # provides zig + the cross toolchains
cargo xtask dist --variant bundle-linux

# …or straight from the flake, no dev shell needed:
nix build .#captain-miao-bundle-linux

Either way it ends with the servers embedded in the finished dashboard, and there is no separate step to run or keep up to date.

The resulting binary pushes the right server to any host that's missing one, verifies it runs there before putting it in place, and skips the work on later connects. The embedded binaries target glibc 2.28 (Debian 10, RHEL 8, and newer) and cost about 7 MB (7.6 → 14.2 MB).

What a dashboard carries is fixed when it is built, and miao --version reports it — including each server's digest, which is what tells two builds of the same version apart. cargo xtask dist builds the named release variants side by side — a plain miao carrying nothing and a miao-bundle-linux carrying both — and --list shows the rest, including single-arch bundles if your fleet is only one. The flake exposes the same set as packages (captain-miao-bundle-linux, -x86_64, -aarch64). Binaries from npm and GitHub Releases are the plain build; each release also publishes the servers on their own, which is what --from release downloads.

miao --version says what any given binary is carrying:

miao 0.2.1
embedded miao-server:
  aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu     3.2 MiB  36fd6ac00444
  x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu      3.4 MiB  c1a3cd563639

On any Linux host that runs the daemon — including your own machine under pooled = true — run loginctl enable-linger:

loginctl enable-linger "$USER"

Without it, systemd-logind removes /run/user/<uid> when you log out, taking the daemon's sockets with it (and on distros with KillUserProcesses=yes, killing the daemon outright). captain-miao recovers on the next login — the daemon notices its socket is gone and rebinds — but linger avoids the outage entirely, which matters precisely when you're away and expecting persistence.

How it works

captain-miao is built around a strict unidirectional data flow:

  • The launcher wraps each agent process and is the single source of truth for that session's state. It receives hook events over a Unix socket and writes a JSON state file.
  • Hooks are thin forwarders: they parse the agent's hook payload from stdin and send it to the launcher socket.
  • The dashboard is a pure viewer. It watches the session state directory and per-backend transcript dirs with notify (FSEvents on macOS, inotify on Linux) and re-reads files when they change. It performs no IPC of its own.

State lives under ~/.local/state/captain-miao/ and runtime sockets under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/captain-miao/, both owner-only: session state files record your prompt text, so they are written 0600 under a 0700 directory. For a deeper tour of the architecture, module layout, hook wiring, and data files, see AGENTS.md.

Roadmap

  • Remote hosts over SSH: one dashboard federating sessions across several machines, with per-host pty pools so remote sessions survive ssh drops, laptop sleep, and dashboard restarts. The full lifecycle — open, resume, attach, detach, steal, kill, restart, fork, auto-reattach on reconnect — is implemented behind the remote cargo feature (cargo build --release --features remote); what's left is verifying it end to end against a real host, so it stays off by default until then. Design notes: docs/remote-sessions.md.
  • More agent backends: the per-session backend is an abstraction, so other coding agents (Kimi Code, opencode, Grok, …) can slot in alongside Claude Code and Codex.
  • More terminal backends: the terminal layer is an abstraction (Kitty and zellij today), so other terminals and multiplexers (tmux, WezTerm, …) can slot in.

also enabled by CAPTAIN_MIAO_DEBUG=1 log_file = "debug.log" keybind_log_file = "keybinds.log" [keybinds] # Remap any Normal-mode command: command-id = "key" or ["key", "alt"]; [] unbinds. # command-ids are the Command::id() strings in src/app/keymap.rs (DEFAULTS table). # e.g. kill = "X" / jump_attention = ["s", "n"] / restart = "space r" Colors accept named values (cyan, dark_gray, …) or #rrggbb hex. The command ids for [keybinds] are the ones in the key-bindings table above (kill, jump_attention, restart, toggle_preview, …). Pooled sessions ([launcher] pooled) By default a session is its terminal window: closing the window ends it. With pooled = true captain-miao instead runs each session in a local pty pool (an embedded libshpool), and the window merely attaches to it — so the session survives closing the window, a crashed multiplexer, and logging out. This is meant for dev servers, not laptops. On a machine you only ever sit at, the pool buys no persistence and costs an extra process hop, no scrollback replay when you reattach, and one client at a time. On a machine you also reach from elsewhere it's the point: a dashboard on your laptop and a captain-miao you ssh into from a phone become two clients of the same sessions. Needs miao-server on PATH (it hosts the pool); without it the dashboard says so and falls back to the default behaviour. On Linux, also run loginctl enable-linger — see below. Running sessions on other machines Remote-host support is behind a cargo feature while it's being verified; build with cargo build --release --features remote, then add hosts with Space h. Each host runs a miao-server daemon holding its sessions in a pty pool, and the dashboard attaches local windows to them over ssh, so a dropped connection or a slept laptop detaches windows without touching the sessions — and reconnecting brings them all back. Full design notes: docs/remote-sessions.md. Getting the daemon onto each host. Either install miao-server there yourself (any copy on PATH matching your dashboard's version is used as is, and never touched), or let the dashboard carry one and deploy it for you: # Download this version's published servers and bundle them in — needs only # curl and tar, no cross toolchain: cargo xtask dist --variant bundle-linux --from release # …or cross-compile them from the sources beside you, which is what you want # while changing the server itself: nix develop # provides zig + the cross toolchains cargo xtask dist --variant bundle-linux # …or straight from the flake, no dev shell needed: nix build .#captain-miao-bundle-linux Either way it ends with the servers embedded in the finished dashboard, and there is no separate step to run or keep up to date. The resulting binary pushes the right server to any host that's missing one, verifies it runs there before putting it in place, and skips the work on later connects. The embedded binaries target glibc 2.28 (Debian 10, RHEL 8, and newer) and cost about 7 MB (7.6 → 14.2 MB). What a dashboard carries is fixed when it is built, and miao --version reports it — including each server's digest, which is what tells two builds of the same version apart. cargo xtask dist builds the named release variants side by side — a plain miao carrying nothing and a miao-bundle-linux carrying both — and --list shows the rest, including single-arch bundles if your fleet is only one. The flake exposes the same set as packages (captain-miao-bundle-linux, -x86_64, -aarch64). Binaries from npm and GitHub Releases are the plain build; each release also publishes the servers on their own, which is what --from release downloads. miao --version says what any given binary is carrying: miao 0.2.1 embedded miao-server: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu 3.2 MiB 36fd6ac00444 x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu 3.4 MiB c1a3cd563639 On any Linux host that runs the daemon — including your own machine under pooled = true — run loginctl enable-linger: loginctl enable-linger "$USER" Without it, systemd-logind removes /run/user/<uid> when you log out, taking the daemon's sockets with it (and on distros with KillUserProcesses=yes, killing the daemon outright). captain-miao recovers on the next login — the daemon notices its socket is gone and rebinds — but linger avoids the outage entirely, which matters precisely when you're away and expecting persistence. How it works captain-miao is built around a strict unidirectional data flow: The launcher wraps each agent process and is the single source of truth for that session's state. It receives hook events over a Unix socket and writes a JSON state file. Hooks are thin forwarders: they parse the agent's hook payload from stdin and send it to the launcher socket. The dashboard is a pure viewer. It watches the session state directory and per-backend transcript dirs with notify (FSEvents on macOS, inotify on Linux) and re-reads files when they change. It performs no IPC of its own. State lives under ~/.local/state/captain-miao/ and runtime sockets under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/captain-miao/, both owner-only: session state files record your prompt text, so they are written 0600 under a 0700 directory. For a deeper tour of the architecture, module layout, hook wiring, and data files, see AGENTS.md. Roadmap Remote hosts over SSH: one dashboard federating sessions across several machines, with per-host pty pools so remote sessions survive ssh drops, laptop sleep, and dashboard restarts. The full lifecycle — open, resume, attach, detach, steal, kill, restart, fork, auto-reattach on reconnect — is implemented behind the remote cargo feature (cargo build --release --features remote); what's left is verifying it end to end against a real host, so it stays off by default until then. Design notes: docs/remote-sessions.md. More agent backends: the per-session backend is an abstraction, so other coding agents (Kimi Code, opencode, Grok, …) can slot in alongside Claude Code and Codex. More terminal backends: the terminal layer is an abstraction (Kitty and zellij today), so other terminals and multiplexers (tmux, WezTerm, …) can slot in. License MIT. See LICENSE.

content_html_zh:
TUI 仪表板，用于管理在您选择的终端模拟器或多路复用器（例如 Kitty 和 zellij）中运行的多个 AI 编码会话。

captain-miao.demo.mp4

当您同时运行多个代理会话时，很难判断哪个正在工作，哪个正在等待您，哪个已经完成。 Captain-miao 监视每个会话并一目了然地显示整个舰队（状态、工作目录、上下文使用情况和实时预览），并让您无需离开仪表板即可启动、聚焦、分叉或终止其中任何一个。

与 herdr 或 cmux 不同，captain-miao 没有嵌入自己的终端。 它驱动您已经运行的 Kitty 或 zellij（每个会话都是一个本机窗口或窗格，通过终端自己的协议进行控制），因此它仍然是一个小型、集中的工具，其余的工作流程由您来编写。

亮点

  • 整个队列一目了然：每个会话都在一个表中，包含状态、工作目录、模型、上下文使用情况、git 分支和实时脚本预览。
  • 永远不会错过提示：等待您批准或答复的会话会被标记。
  • 完整的会话生命周期：从仪表板启动、恢复、分叉和终止会话，并使用最近工作目录的可过滤选择器。
  • 立即支持 Claude Code 和 Codex，其背后是为扩展到其他编码代理而构建的后端抽象。
  • direnv-aware：在具有 .envrc 的目录中启动的会话会自动选择该环境（通过 direnv exec）。
  • r3 集成：当会话的运行后台任务是等待您审阅的 r3 监视时，它会标记为“审阅”并显示为需要您注意。
  • 保持清醒：防止您的机器在任何会话仍在工作时进入睡眠状态（macOS 上的咖啡因，Linux 上的 systemd-inhibit）。
  • 固定、静音、标记：将重要的会话固定到顶部，将您现在不需要的会话静音，并标记要跟进的会话。
  • 超出其窗口寿命的会话（选择加入）：在本地 pty 池中运行它们，因此关闭终端（或注销）不会结束它们，并且另一台计算机上的仪表板可以连接到相同的仪表板。

要求

  • 支持的终端：启用远程控制的 Kitty（请参阅 Kitty 设置），或 zellij ≥ 0.44（在 zellij 会话内运行 Captain-miao；无需额外设置）。
  • 您的 PATH 上的 Claude Code 和/或 Codex。

安装

来自 Cargo 的来源

cargo install --git https://github.com/hyperlogue/captain-miao

这将安装 miao 命令（该项目是 Captain-miao；二进制文件很短，因为您会经常键入它）。

构建需要 Rust 工具链和 C 编译器（用于读取 Codex 会话标题的静态捆绑 SQLite）。

来自预构建的二进制文件 (npm)

没有 Rust 工具链，没有构建：

npx @hyperlogue/captain-miao          # run it once
npm install -g @hyperlogue/captain-miao   # or install the `miao` command

Bunx @hyperlogue/captain-miao 也可以。 npm 包是一个小型启动器，它执行作为每个平台可选依赖项提供的预构建本机二进制文件，因此您的包管理器仅下载与您的计算机匹配的一个二进制文件；运行时不会获取任何内容。 预构建的二进制文件涵盖 macOS（Apple Silicon + Intel）和 Linux（x86-64 + arm64），如果您想直接下载，它们也会以 .tar.gz 形式附加到每个 GitHub 版本。

与尼克斯

提供薄片；直接从 GitHub 运行它：

nix run github:hyperlogue/captain-miao

小猫设置

Captain-miao 通过其远程控制协议驱动 Kitty，因此您的 kitty.conf 必须允许它。 远程控制是一种真正的特权（拥有它的程序可以读取您的终端并运行命令），因此最严格的设置 kitty 提供了密码与授权脚本的配对：

allow_remote_control password
remote_control_password "i-am-the-captain-miao" captain_miao_rc.py
listen_on unix:/tmp/mykitty

Kitty 根据您的配置目录解析该文件名，因此将脚本放在 ~/.config/kitty/captain_miao_rc.py 中：

# The only remote-control commands captain-miao issues.
ALLOWED_COMMANDS = frozenset({
    "ls", "get-text", "launch", "focus-window",
    "focus-tab", "close-window", "detach-window", "goto-layout",
})

def is_cmd_allowed(pcmd, window, from_socket, extra_data):
    # Reject the in-terminal escape-code channel; only the listen_on socket gets in.
    return from_socket and pcmd["cmd"] in ALLOWED_COMMANDS

现在每个请求都必须清除三项检查：通过套接字到达（不是 shell 可以使用的转义码通道，即使是跨 ssh 的 shell），携带密码，并命名上述命令之一。 i-am-the-captain-miao 是 Captain-miao 的内置默认值，所以这按写的那样工作；要使用您自己的密码，请在 Captain-miao 的配置中设置 Remote_control_password （上面）和 [kitty] rc_password 进行匹配。 将脚本保留在密码后面的最后一项；允许在其旁边列出命令名称，而无需调用您的函数。

更宽松的替代方案：allow_remote_control仅限套接字（关闭转义码通道，但没有密码，也没有白名单）或allow_remote_control yes（根本不检查；避免它）。 Captain-miao 在启动时验证远程控制，如果无法连接则退出并进行诊断。

保持堆栈布局启用。 Captain-miao 的默认 Stacked 会话布局将每个会话放入一个 kitty 选项卡中，并通过 kitty 的堆栈布局一次显示一个会话。 默认的enabled_layouts * 已经包含它；如果您缩小了该列表的范围，请添加堆栈或会话图块而不是堆栈。 （备用的每选项卡布局，用 Space l 切换，不需要特定的布局。）

Usage

在支持的终端（Kitty 或 zellij）内​​运行仪表板：

miao
miao 必须从 Kitty 或 zellij 会话中启动；否则它将退出并出现错误。 当在 zellij 会话中运行时，它会自动选择 zellij 后端（使用配置中的 [terminal] 后端覆盖）。

在仪表板上，o/O 启动新会话，r 恢复现有会话。 你也可以从 shell 驱动 Captain-miao：

命令 它的作用
miao 运行 TUI 仪表板（默认）。
miao claude [目录] [参数...] 在 dir 中启动 Claude Code（默认）。 带跟踪钩。 以 - 开头的参数（例如 --resume）将直接转发给 claude。
苗法典 [目录] [参数...] 在带有跟踪钩子的目录中启动 Codex；额外的参数被转发到法典。
苗焦点 [--window-id <id>] 聚焦正在运行的仪表板窗口；使用 --window-id，还可以响铃在该 Kitty 窗口中运行的会话。
苗钩<事件> 内部：将代理挂钩事件转发到启动器。 你不会自己运行这个；它会自动连接。

通过 claude / codex 启动的会话由注入跟踪挂钩的启动器进程包装，因此它们会自动显示在仪表板中。 钩子在每次会话时注入并在退出时拆除；没有任何内容写入您的全局 ~/.claude/settings.json。

键绑定

按 ？ 在仪表板中查看完整列表。 亮点：

Key 行动
j/k、↑/↓、Ctrl-n/p 导航会话
gg / G 跳转到顶部/底部
1..9 / Ctrl-1..9 选择第 N 个会话/选择并聚焦其窗口
Enter 聚焦所选会话的窗口
o / O 新会话（相同选项卡/cwd 提示）
r / f 恢复选择器（一台主机；Ctrl-h 切换）/分叉所选会话
x / D 终止选定的会话/与其分离，使其保持运行
s 跳转到下一个需要关注的会话
m / p / i 静音/固定/切换所选会话上的需求输入
y 将选定的会话 ID 复制到剪贴板
t / w 将窗口移动到选项卡（仅限 Kitty）/切换到或打开 cwd 的工作选项卡
h/l, ←/→ 水平滚动预览
Ctrl-u / Ctrl-d 向上/向下滚动预览
R 立即刷新预览
空间 v / 空间 d 切换预览/详细信息面板
空间我 编辑所选目录的图标+颜色
空间 e / 空间 E 重新启动选定/所有空闲会话
空间 z 切换保持唤醒（在会话工作时禁止操作系统睡眠）
空间 a / 空间 H 为新会话设置默认后端/默认主机
空间l 切换会话布局（堆叠在一个选项卡中/每个会话一个选项卡）
空间 h / 空间 s 主机面板/附加到会话，踢出持有它的客户端
? 显示完整的按键列表（帮助覆盖）
/ 搜索
q / Ctrl-c Quit

按空格键（前导键）会在页脚中显示可用后续键的哪个键条。

在 cwd 选择器中，Ctrl-t 切换该启动的后端，Ctrl-h 切换主机，Ctrl-d 删除突出显示的最近目录。

自定义键绑定。 上面的每个普通模式命令都可以通过 ~/.config/captain-miao/config.toml 中的 [keybinds] 表重新映射。 将命令 ID 映射到键（或键列表）；空列表会解除它的绑定：

[keybinds]
kill = "X"                      # move kill from x to X
jump_attention = ["s", "n"]     # bind two keys to one command
restart = "space r"             # remap a leader sequence
toggle_detail = []              # unbind a command

键解析“ctrl+u”、“O”（=“shift+o”）、“space e”、“enter”、“f5”和箭头名称等形式。 Ctrl-c、g g 和 1..9 / Ctrl-1..9 选择器已修复。

命令 ids 是每个 Command::id(); 中的字符串；权威列表位于 src/app/keymap.rs 中的 DEFAULTS 表中，它们与上面的键绑定表中的操作相匹配。

配置

Captain-miao 读取 ~/.config/captain-miao/config.toml （或 $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/captain-miao/config.toml）中的可选 TOML 文件。 每个键都是可选的，并回退到如下所示的默认值；无法解析的文件会恢复到默认值而不是崩溃。 完整的选项集：

[terminal]
backend = "kitty"            # "kitty" | "zellij"; unset auto-detects (zellij inside a zellij session, else Kitty)
sessions_layout = "stacked"  # "stacked" | "per-tab" (the runtime Space l toggle overrides this)

[kitty]
rc_password = "i-am-the-captain-miao"   # the built-in default, and a published constant; set your own (see Kitty setup)

[launcher]
default_agent = "claude"     # backend for new sessions: "claude" | "codex" (Space a overrides)
approval_grace_secs = 2      # grace window after a permission dialog before a transcript change reads as "dismissed"
max_recent_cwds = 50         # entries kept in the workdir picker's recent list
resume_list_limit = 200      # max sessions listed in the resume picker
new_tab_title = "{agent}: {basename}"     # new-session tab title; placeholders: {agent} {basename} {cwd}
resume_tab_title = "{agent}: {basename}"  # resumed-session tab title
pooled = false               # run this machine's sessions in the local pty pool (see below)

[thresholds]
context_warning_tokens = 175000    # context usage turns to the warning color here
context_critical_tokens = 400000   # …and to the critical color here
preview_stale_secs = 20            # show "updated Ns ago" once the preview is older than this (0 = always)

[polling]
fs_reload_debounce_ms = 100        # debounce for filesystem-watch reloads
preview_debounce_ms = 200          # debounce before re-fetching the preview
event_poll_ms = 100                # input poll interval (floored at 10)
preview_auto_refresh_secs = 10     # auto-refresh the preview while focused + busy + unscrolled (0 disables)

[ui.panels]
preview_auto_min_height = 16       # min body height before the preview auto-shows
detail_auto_min_width = 70         # min body width before the detail panel auto-shows
detail_default_width = 36          # detail panel column width
narrow_max_width = 90              # at/below this body width the layout stacks vertically

[ui.table]
name_truncate = 35                 # max characters of a session name before truncation

[colors.ui]
title_fg = "cyan"
header_fg = "cyan"
attention_fg = "yellow"
error_fg = "red"
highlight_bg = "dark_gray"
selection_fg = "blue"
selection_symbol = "❯ "

[colors.picker]
highlight_bg = "dark_gray"
chevron_fg = "blue"

[debug]
enabled = false                    # verbose logging; also enabled by CAPTAIN_MIAO_DEBUG=1
log_file = "debug.log"
keybind_log_file = "keybinds.log"

[keybinds]

# command-ids are the Command::id() strings in src/app/keymap.rs (DEFAULTS table).
# e.g. kill = "X"  /  jump_attention = ["s", "n"]  /  restart = "space r"

颜色接受命名值（青色、暗灰色……） 或#rrggbb 十六进制。 [keybinds] 的命令 ID 是上面键绑定表中的命令 ID（kill、jump_attention、restart、toggle_preview 等）。

池化会话（[启动器]池化）

默认情况下，会话是其终端窗口：关闭窗口将结束它。 使用 pooled = true Captain-miao 则在本地 pty 池（嵌入式 libshpool）中运行每个会话，并且窗口仅附加到它 - 因此会话在关闭窗口、崩溃的多路复用器和注销后仍然存在。

这适用于开发服务器，而不是笔记本电脑。 在您只坐过的一台机器上，池不会购买持久性，并且会花费额外的进程跳跃，重新连接时不会回滚重播，并且一次只有一个客户端。 在一台你也可以从其他地方访问的机器上，重点是：你笔记本电脑上的仪表板和你从手机上 ssh 到的 Captain-miao 成为同一会话的两个客户端。

需要 PATH 上的 miao-server （它托管池）；如果没有它，仪表板会这样显示并回退到默认行为。 在 Linux 上，还运行 loginctl enable-linger — 见下文。

在其他机器上运行会话

正在验证货物功能背后的远程主机支持；使用 Cargo build --release --features Remote 进行构建，然后使用 Space h 添加主机。 每个主机都运行一个 miao-server 守护进程，将其会话保存在 pty 池中，并且仪表板通过 ssh 将本地窗口附加到它们，因此断开的连接或睡眠的笔记本电脑会分离窗口而不触及会话 - 重新连接会将它们全部恢复。 完整的设计说明：docs/remote-sessions.md。

将守护进程安装到每台主机上。 要么自己安装 miao-server （路径上与您的仪表板版本匹配的任何副本都按原样使用，并且从未触及），或者让仪表板携带一个并为您部署它：

# Download this version's published servers and bundle them in — needs only
# curl and tar, no cross toolchain:
cargo xtask dist --variant bundle-linux --from release

# …or cross-compile them from the sources beside you, which is what you want
# while changing the server itself:
nix develop                                # provides zig + the cross toolchains
cargo xtask dist --variant bundle-linux

# …or straight from the flake, no dev shell needed:
nix build .#captain-miao-bundle-linux

无论哪种方式，它都会以嵌入完成的仪表板中的服务器结束，并且没有单独的步骤来运行或保持最新。

生成的二进制文件将正确的服务器推送到任何缺少服务器的主机，在将其安装到位之前验证它是否在那里运行，并跳过稍后连接的工作。 嵌入式二进制文件以 glibc 2.28（Debian 10、RHEL 8 及更高版本）为目标，成本约为 7 MB (7.6 → 14.2 MB)。

仪表板所携带的内容在构建时是固定的，并且 miao --version 会报告它 - 包括每个服务器的摘要，这可以区分同一版本的两个构建。 Cargo xtask dist 并排构建指定的版本变体 - 一个普通的 miao 不携带任何内容，而一个 miao-bundle-linux 携带两者 - 并且 --list 显示其余部分，包括单架构捆绑包（如果您的舰队只有一个）。 该薄片公开了与包相同的集合（captain-miao-bundle-linux、-x86_64、-aarch64）。 来自 npm 和 GitHub Releases 的二进制文件是普通构建；每个版本还自行发布服务器，这就是从版本下载中获得的内容。

miao --version 表示任何给定的二进制文件所携带的内容：

miao 0.2.1
embedded miao-server:
  aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu     3.2 MiB  36fd6ac00444
  x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu      3.4 MiB  c1a3cd563639

在任何运行守护进程的 Linux 主机上——包括你自己的在 pooled = true 下的机器——运行 loginctl enable-linger：

loginctl enable-linger "$USER"

如果没有它，当您注销时，systemd-logind 会删除 /run/user/<uid> ，并带走守护进程的套接字（在带有 KillUserProcesses=yes 的发行版上，直接杀死守护进程）。 Captain-miao 在下次登录时恢复 - 守护进程注意到它的套接字已消失并重新绑定 - 但 linger 完全避免了中断，这在您离开并期待持久性时非常重要。

它是如何运作的

Captain-miao 是围绕严格的单向数据流构建的：

  • 启动器包装每个代理进程，并且是该会话状态的唯一事实来源。 它通过 Unix 套接字接收挂钩事件并写入 JSON 状态文件。
  • 钩子是瘦转发器：它们从标准输入解析代理的钩子有效负载并将其发送到启动器套接字。
  • 仪表板是一个纯粹的查看器。 它通过通知（macOS 上的 FSEvents，Linux 上的 inotify）监视会话状态目录和每个后端转录目录，并在文件发生更改时重新读取文件。 它自己不执行 IPC。

状态位于 ~/.local/state/captain-miao/ 下，运行时套接字位于 $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/captain-miao/ 下，两者均为所有者：会话状态文件记录您的提示文本，因此它们在 0700 目录下写入 0600。 要更深入地了解架构、模块布局、挂钩接线和数据文件，请参阅 AGENTS.md。

路线图

  • 通过 SSH 的远程主机：一个仪表板联合多台计算机上的会话，并具有每个主机 pty 池，因此远程会话可以在 ssh 丢失、笔记本电脑睡眠和仪表板重新启动的情况下继续存在。 完整的生命周期——打开、恢复、附加、分离、窃取、终止、重新启动、分叉、重新连接时自动重新附加——是在远程货物功能（货物构建-释放-功能远程）背后实现的；剩下的就是针对真实主机进行端到端验证，因此在此之前它默认保持关闭状态。 设计说明：docs/remote-sessions.md。
  • 更多代理后端：每个会话后端是一个抽象，因此其他编码代理（Kimi Code、opencode、Grok 等） 可以与 Claude Code 和 Codex 一起插入。
  • 更多终端后端：终端层是一个抽象（今天的 Kitty 和 zellij），因此其他终端和多路复用器（tmux、WezTerm 等） 可以插进去。
